---
title: Search your app's data
description: Declare which fields of a collection are indexed, query them from a view, and know what it costs, what it guarantees and where it stops.
sidebar:
  order: 6
---

**Task:** find records by the words in them — notes that mention "invoice",
titles that start with "roa" — without reading every record in the app.

Each node that holds a replica of the app keeps a full-text index
([tantivy](https://github.com/quickwit-oss/tantivy)) of the tables that declare
search fields, in memory, built from the state it holds. The index is derived
data: it is never replicated, never written to disk, and never part of the
app's state. A query reads the page of hits, never the table.

## Declare and query

Declare the fields to index on the table itself, and the host keeps the index
from the app's state:

```rust
#[derive(Record)]
#[table(key = "id", search = ["title", "body"])]
pub struct Note {
    pub id: String,
    pub title: String,
    pub body: String,
}

#[app::view]
pub fn find_notes(&self, text: String) -> app::Result<Vec<Note>> {
    let found = self.notes.search(&text, SearchOpts::default().limit(20))?;
    Ok(found.items.into_iter().map(|f| f.record).collect())
}
```

- The state ABI lists the fields (`state.search`: table to fields, camelCase).
  Text fields are indexed; a list of strings is joined; anything else is skipped.
- Every record of the table is one document. Each replica derives its index
  from the record keys the entries it applied touched, else from a scan of the
  table, before a view reads; nothing enters the log.
- `Table::search(text, SearchOpts)` queries through the WIT `search` interface
  (`SearchMode::{Words, Prefix, Substring, Fuzzy}`, a cursor and a limit of 1 to
  100) and reads each hit's record back; a hit whose record is gone is skipped.
  Only views search; any other run traps `HostDenied`. A call of a declared view
  runs as a strong view, so it may search too.
- The test harness (`TestApp`) answers searches with a plain scan: records whose
  declared fields contain every word of the query, all scored the same. Assert
  which records match, not their order.

## Limits

- One index per table, over the fields its `#[table(search = [..])]` names.
- A query is at most 256 bytes and 4 KiB encoded; a page at most 100 hits; a
  cursor at most 10,000 deep.
- Fuzzy matching is edit distance 1 on words: no stemming, no synonyms, no
  phonetics. Substring search needs 3 characters.
- Scores are per app (each index has its own term statistics).
- A stale view on a replica that is behind searches the state that replica
  has applied.
- A new release rebuilds the indexes from state, on the first view after it,
  about 0.1 ms a document. So does the first view after a restart or after the
  app moves to a node: indexes that survive a restart are not done yet.

## Operating it

There is nothing to configure: search is on for every app that declares an
index, and its indexes live in memory on the nodes that serve its views. A
node keeps the touched entities of the last 4096 entries per app
(`TOUCHED_RING`); a view after a longer gap rebuilds from a scan.
